constraints: Decision must be grounded in the provided benchmark evidence.
Avoid recommending infrastructure before measuring the dominant bottleneck.
core_question: Determine whether query-path consolidation (JOIN) or caching (Redis) should be tested first based on the executable benchmark evidence.
knowns: Team proposes Redis as a solution.
Executable benchmark code measures two SQLite query paths: N+1 (51 queries) and JOIN (1 query).
Benchmark ran 200 runs per strategy on an in-memory SQLite database with 50 accounts.
N+1 strategy: query_count=51, row_count=50, median_duration_us=49.041, p95_duration_us=56.833.
JOIN strategy: query_count=1, row_count=50, median_duration_us=9.583, p95_duration_us=11.709.
success_criteria: The chosen first test targets the measured dominant bottleneck (N+1 query count).
Evidence shows whether query consolidation alone meets latency targets before adding caching.
unknowns: Production database latency characteristics (network, disk, concurrency).
Dashboard query complexity beyond the measured accounts+details pattern.
Cache invalidation requirements and data freshness needs.
Whether Redis would be applied to the N+1 path or the JOIN path.
Team's operational capacity to run and maintain Redis.
